summary_html: Cases arising on **federal lands/facilities** or involving **Indian children** invoke federal/tribal jurisdictional rules (VICAA for federal facilities; **ICWA** for Indian children and tribal preference/jurisdiction).
authority_html:
- **VICAA (34 U.S.C. §§ 20301–20307)** — federal-facility reporting mandates  
- **ICWA (25 U.S.C. §§ 1901–1963)** — tribal jurisdiction, placement preferences, notice to tribes

primary_citations.citation_text: Maryland - Md. Code, Family Law Article §§ 5-701 et seq. (Child Abuse and Neglect; definitions at § 5-701, mandatory reporting at §§ 5-704 and 5-705, investigation at § 5-706, appeal of findings at § 5-706.1)
Maryland - Courts & Judicial Proc. § 3-801 et seq. (CINA—Child in Need of Assistance proceedings)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Court held that ICWA's 'active efforts' requirement is satisfied by substantive proof that the department made, and exhausted, remedial and rehabilitative efforts, and that the juvenile court need not recite the statute's wording; it reversed the intermediate court and directed that the circuit court judgment be affirmed.
key_cases.relevance: This is Maryland's only high-court decision applying the Indian Child Welfare Act in a CINA case and it defines what triggers and satisfies the federal standard.
key_cases.quote: what is important is whether the Department in substance made active efforts to prevent the breakup of the family, whether those efforts were unsuccessful

key_cases.case_name: Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians v. Holyfield
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court reversed a Mississippi adoption decree, holding that 'domicile' under ICWA is a matter of uniform federal law, that children born off-reservation to reservation-domiciled parents were themselves domiciled on the reservation, and that the tribal court therefore had exclusive jurisdiction under 25 U.S.C. § 1911(a).
key_cases.relevance: It is the controlling federal decision on when an Indian child's case belongs exclusively to a tribal court, the jurisdictional question Maryland's sole ICWA decision leaves undecided.
key_cases.quote: In enacting the ICWA Congress confirmed that, in child custody proceedings involving Indian children domiciled on the reservation, tribal jurisdiction was exclusive as to the States.

mandatory_reporters: Any person (universal mandatory reporting) — Md. Code, Fam. Law § 5-705(a)(1)
Health practitioners — Md. Code, Fam. Law § 5-704(a)
Police officers — Md. Code, Fam. Law § 5-704(a)
Educators or human service workers, including teachers, counselors, social workers, caseworkers, and probation or parole officers — Md. Code, Fam. Law §§ 5-704(a), 5-701(g)
Narrow exceptions to the any-person duty: attorney-client privilege, the constitutional right to counsel, and certain clergy confidences — Md. Code, Fam. Law § 5-705(a)(2)-(3)
reporting_details: Maryland is a universal-reporter state: any person who has reason to believe a child has been abused or neglected must notify the local department of social services or the appropriate law enforcement agency, and a health practitioner, police officer, educator, or human service worker must also file a written report with the local department not later than 48 hours after the contact, with a copy to the local State's Attorney (Md. Code, Fam. Law §§ 5-704, 5-705).

timeline_requirements.deadline: 24 hours (suspected physical or sexual abuse); 5 days (suspected neglect or mental injury)
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Report received by the local department or the appropriate law enforcement agency
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in Md. Code, Fam. Law § 5-706

timeline_requirements.deadline: 10 days to the extent possible; if not completed within 30 days, within 60 days
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of the first notice of the suspected abuse or neglect
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in Md. Code, Fam. Law § 5-706
